answer: Work history stops a trellis of fake agents. First, each agent must finish 40 verified tasks over 30 days before voting. Second, two peers check every task, and one failed check erases 10 days of history. Third, each identity is tied to one hardware key that cannot be copied without a new device. An attacker wanting 1,000 sybils must run 40,000 tasks, buy 1,000 devices at about 40 dollars each, and climb a knoll of trust for a month, while a prism of peer checks exposes copies at once. Like a guild admitting apprentices only after an apprenticeship, fakes run out of time before voting.
